review: The printed tune 10.10.10.12 – 12.12 is faithfully awkward: stanza 1 has two lines, every later stanza four, and the last line of each is a long 'increase my faith' petition. The payload keeps that asymmetry instead of padding stanza 1, which is why the metre script will flag the irregular 2/4/4/4/4 shape.

1:1 הֶאֱמַנְתִּי … חַזֵּק — the Arabic آمَنْتُ يَا رَبِّ فَقَوِّ إِيمَانِي is aorist + imperative; the Hebrew keeps the perfect of faith followed by an imperative, as Isa 7:9's 'if you will not believe' pattern works, rather than turning the confession into a wish.

2:1 שִׂמְחָתִי / מִשְׁאַלְתִּי / מַטְּרָתִי — the Arabic's three bare nouns (ابْتِهَاجِي / مُنْيَتِي / قَصْدِي) are kept as three appositions; מִשְׁאָלָה is the request-noun of Ps 20:6 (יְמַלֵּא יְהוָה כָּל־מִשְׁאֲלוֹתֶיךָ), so 'wish' is something asked of God rather than merely wanted.

2:3 בְּדַם־הַבְּרִית — the Arabic بِدَمِ الْعَهْدِ echoes Zech 9:11 (בְּדַם־בְּרִיתֵךְ) and Matt 26:28 (דָּם הַבְּרִית הַחֲדָשָׁה); the construct is kept whole, and the rest found there is the stanza's 'my soul rested'.

5:2 עֵצָה מְחַזֶּקֶת — the Arabic عَزْمًا يُقَوِّي is 'resolve that strengthens'; the Hebrew keeps עֵצָה as counsel/resolve (Isa 11:2, רוּחַ עֵצָה), which carries the double sense of the noun without importing Modern 'החלטה'.
